title: ANYBODY, ANYWHERE
summary: Pairs of strangers doing related things, side by side, each half with its own sound and its own date. 1961 and 1944 prepare a place to sit; one has sat down and the other has left the chairs empty. Iraq 1951 lights a fire in silence beside an American kitchen film talking about productivity. Two people sweep.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: inconclusive, leaning reference stronger. I can't hear the film, so the sound-space criterion is unjudged.

Noticed before the brief: at 0:03-0:11 a man bends to arrange theatre chairs while a woman's hands tilt and then sit on a swivel chair. The two are cut in alternating one-second steps. Both are "preparing a seat", and the narration ("chair should have a firm back support", 0:00-0:05) rhymes with both. That alignment is clear and earned.

Largest gap: the film never reaches the "different outcome" it was built for. The 0:17-0:34 pairs are Iraq 1951 crouching on straw / kitchen, then sweeping / sweeping. All of it is cut at a steady one-second alternation, so the mismatch doesn't register as a mismatch. There is no wider context shot (the brief's "restore a wider view") and no final hold. The last frames (0:32-0:34) just keep cutting between brooms, so the ending feels the same as the opening. The people are not set apart as particular lives. The 1957 magenta clip at 0:29 and 0:31 reads as glitch, not information. At 34 seconds, the film is far short of the 90-second target. The small caption text is unreadable at this size, so the date states cannot be judged.

Repairs:
1. 0:12-0:16: one side drops to a black or empty frame (0:15, 0:16) while the other holds. Condition: replace it with a shot of the person finishing or waiting.
2. 0:29-0:31: the 1957 pink clip. Condition: either it carries a legible date and place card, or it is cut.
3. 0:32-0:34: end on a single held wide frame of one pair for 3 seconds or more. Condition: the shot ends the cutting rhythm that came before it.

Strength to protect: the chair pair at 0:03-0:11, where the cuts, the narration and the gesture all agree.
reviews.builder_note: The critic read the two halves as alternating one-second cuts. They play at the same time, each with its own sound. Date labels were too small: enlarged. The film now ends on a held pair. A wider context shot and dropping the 1957 clip were not done.
